name: Galaxy Digital Inc.
founded: 2018 (Galaxy Digital Holdings Ltd., Cayman Islands); Galaxy Digital Inc. incorporated in Delaware 23 April 2021, successor public company from 13 May 2025
employees: 700+ worldwide, ~530 in the United States (31 December 2025)
summary:
**BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** Galaxy Digital is a digital-asset financial-services firm that also owns one of the largest single-site data-centre campuses in ERCOT, and the two halves are not comparable businesses. The SEC classifies it under SIC 6211, Security Brokers, Dealers and Flotation Companies; it reports FY2025 revenue of **USD 60.41bn** on a gross principal basis — trading turnover, not rent — against total equity of USD 3.03bn and a net loss of USD 241.3m. Its Helios campus in Dickens County, Texas holds 1.63 GW of ERCOT-approved power, of which **800 MW gross / 526 MW of critical IT load is leased to CoreWeave and nothing else is leased to anyone**. Phase I's 133 MW of critical IT load was fully delivered by 30 June 2026 and is expected to run at about USD 80m of quarterly leasing revenue from Q3 2026; Phases II and III follow in 2027 and 2028. Filed under `developer` for what Helios is, the company's balance sheet, revenue model and risk register are a financial institution's.

**BACKGROUND.** Delaware-incorporated, New York-headquartered, listed on Nasdaq as GLXY and, since 19 March 2026, on no other exchange — the company voluntarily delisted from the Toronto Stock Exchange, though it remains a reporting issuer in Canada filing on SEDAR. The structure is an Up-C: Galaxy Digital Inc. is the general partner of Galaxy Digital Holdings LP, which conducts the business; Class B common stock carries votes but no economic interest, and **both classes carry one vote per share** — there is no super-voting class. Founder and chief executive Michael Novogratz held about **49.25% of total voting power** at 2 April 2026. Three reportable segments since Q1 2025: Digital Assets, Data Centers, and Treasury and Corporate. FY2025 adjusted EBITDA was USD 33.7m against USD 715.4m in FY2024; the swing is a USD 753.7m digital-asset impairment charge and about USD 160m of one-time costs. Equity capital at 30 June 2026 was allocated roughly 36% Digital Assets, 36% Data Centers and 28% Treasury and Corporate — the data centre now consumes as much of the firm's capital as its original business.
ecosystemRole: The corpus's first data-centre owner that is not, in any other respect, a data-centre company. Galaxy sits in the `developer` category beside Digital Realty, CyrusOne, Compass, EdgeCore, Prime and the converted miners, and it competes with them for ERCOT interconnection capacity and for the same neocloud and hyperscaler demand. But its revenue is principally trading turnover, its largest counterparty exposures are lending and trading counterparties rather than tenants, and its regulator treats it as a securities broker-dealer. For the ecosystem it is therefore two things at once: a landlord whose single tenant is CoreWeave — the same counterparty that anchors Core Scientific and Applied Digital — and a capital-markets participant that finances, advises and takes positions in the digital-asset businesses several other dossiers in this corpus describe. Its power counterparties are AEP Texas and Wind Energy Transmission Texas; its exposure to Governor Abbott's August 2026 data-centre audit is disclosed in its own 10-Q as a risk to power approval timelines.

productsAndServices.name: Global Markets — trading, lending, derivatives and investment banking
productsAndServices.description: Galaxy's original and still largest earning business, and the source of the USD 60.41bn revenue line that dominates its accounts. Galaxy trades digital assets **as principal**, so the gross proceeds of every sale are recognised as revenue with an almost exactly offsetting cost in Transaction expenses — FY2025 revenue of USD 60,406.7m against transaction expenses of USD 60,175.8m. Digital-asset sales alone were USD 59,850.9m of that, and a single Q3 2025 trade of **80,000 BTC** is named by the company as the principal driver of the year-on-year increase. Bitcoin, ether and tether were 85% of digital-asset sales in FY2025. Alongside the trading desk sit a collateralised lending book (average USD 1,794.8m in FY2025, USD 1,438m in Q2 2026, typically 110-140% collateralised), an OTC derivatives business with a registered swap dealer, and an investment bank whose largest FY2025 fee came from acting as placement agent on the Forward Industries Solana-treasury PIPE.
highlights: 1,741 trading counterparties at Q2 2026, from 1,381 at Q1 2025

Revenue is recognised gross because Galaxy acts as principal — the company itself warns that 'the magnitude of changes in Revenue on the Company's statement of operations overshadow other parts of the business, but are predominantly offset by Transaction expenses in Net income'
Global Markets adjusted gross profit: USD 294.5m in Q3 2025 (a record, including a USD 9bn notional bitcoin sale), then USD 30m, USD 31m and USD 49m in the three quarters to Q2 2026

Three FINRA broker-dealers (Galaxy Digital Partners, Galaxy Securities, FIN2), an SEC-registered adviser, a CFTC CTA/CPO, a registered swap dealer and an FCA-licensed UK entity; Galaxy claims more than 50 global licences
NYDFS granted GalaxyOne Prime NY a BitLicense and Money Transmission License on 18 May 2026 — Galaxy held no BitLicense at the date of the FY2025 10-K
Concentration disclosed in the 10-K: two digital-asset trading platforms accounted for 38% of FY2025 revenue, and three counterparties for 45% of the combined loans receivable balance
productsAndServices.positioning: Against Coinbase, Cumberland/DRW, FalconX and B2C2, Galaxy is a full-service merchant bank rather than a pure exchange or market maker. No independent league table of digital-asset OTC desks with market shares could be located, so its rank in trading is unmeasured. In lending it is roughly the size of Coinbase — about USD 1bn to USD 1.4bn of book against a CeFi market of about USD 23.3bn in Q1 2026 in which Tether alone holds about 68% — so mid-single-digit share, not leadership.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct institutional relationships; principal trading, bilateral lending and advisory mandates. GalaxyOne, launched October 2025, adds a retail channel with an FDIC-insured deposit account through Cross River Bank, equities through DriveWealth and crypto through Paxos.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Galaxy Onchain Financing Rate (GOFR) launched 14 July 2026; institutional OTC prediction markets from 2 June 2026; an Institutional Vault Curator from 16 July 2026; a Crypto Portfolio Line of Credit from 25 August 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Data Centers — the Helios campus and the CoreWeave leases
productsAndServices.description: A 2,200-plus-acre campus in Dickens County, Texas, bought from Argo Blockchain in December 2022 as a bitcoin mining facility and converted after mining ceased at the end of Q1 2025. Galaxy publishes three power numbers that must not be conflated: **1.63 GW is ERCOT-approved and utility-contracted**, **800 MW gross / 526 MW critical IT is leased to CoreWeave**, and **133 MW of critical IT was delivered and in service at 30 June 2026**. The CoreWeave capacity comes in three phases on identical terms — 15-year base leases with two five-year extension options, a 3.0-5.0% CPI-linked escalator, and a near-triple-net structure in which the tenant pays operating costs but Galaxy provides the personnel. Phase I (133 MW IT / ~200 MW gross) delivered its first data hall in April 2026 and was complete by quarter end; Phase II (260 MW IT / ~400 MW gross, lease dated 8 August 2025) begins delivering in Q2 2027 with HITT Contracting as general contractor; Phase III (133 MW IT / ~200 MW gross, lease entered January 2026) is due in 2028. The remaining 830 MW of approved capacity is unleased and Galaxy says discussions with prospective tenants continue.
highlights: **One tenant, and the 10-K says so**: 'We expect that our AI/HPC data center business will initially be highly dependent on a single customer, CoreWeave' — 100% of contracted capacity, with the initial contract expiring in 2040

Galaxy publishes no all-phase base-term contract value. It publishes about USD 4.5bn of total lease payments for Phase I alone, USD 10.4bn of minimum contracted lease payments for Phase II alone, and 'more than USD 1.2bn' of anticipated **average annual** revenue across all three — raised from 'USD 1B+' in the Q1 2026 release
The audited figure is different again: ASC 842 total future minimum lease income of **USD 4,747.8m** at 30 June 2026
Phase II starting gross yield on cost 13.7%; Phase I capex about USD 13m per MW of critical IT load, about USD 1.75bn in total; lease-level adjusted EBITDA margins guided at about 90%+
Phase I is expected to run at about USD 80m of quarterly leasing revenue from Q3 2026
Design: 130-140 kW rack densities, closed-loop cooling requiring near-zero additional water after the initial fill, under 15 ms round trip to Dallas, Galaxy-owned private substation
Pipeline beyond Helios: Merlin at McGregor (500 acres, 74 MW initial phase, potential 500 MW), Caspian (~700 MW) and Selene (~900 MW), taking the stated company power pipeline above 5.7 GW
productsAndServices.positioning: Helios competes with Cipher's Texas campuses, Hut 8's Beacon Point, TeraWulf, Core Scientific and Applied Digital for ERCOT interconnection and for neocloud demand. On counterparty credit it is at the weak end of that set: CoreWeave is unrated and levered, and unlike Cipher (Amazon.com guaranty) or Hut 8 (an undisclosed high-investment-grade tenant plus a Google backstop at River Bend) Galaxy discloses no credit enhancement behind its single tenant. On measured scale it is mid-pack at 526 MW of critical IT.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct long-term leases; DLA Piper acted for Galaxy on the Phase I lease and option agreement.
targetSegments: Hyperscale cloud providers (for the unleased 830 MW)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Phase II data-hall deliveries from Q2 2027; Phase III in 2028; Helios III and Helios IV load requests of 1 GW each in the ERCOT process, which Galaxy says would take the campus to a potential 3.6 GW; Merlin first power in 2028.

productsAndServices.name: Asset Management and Infrastructure Solutions
productsAndServices.description: Galaxy manages funds and sub-advises exchange-traded products, and runs validator infrastructure for proof-of-stake networks. The platform is measured in two ways the company reports separately: assets under management across ETFs and Alternatives, and assets under stake. **The combined figure has more than halved in six months** — from about USD 12bn of total platform assets at the end of 2025 to USD 7.1bn at 30 June 2026, with ETFs at USD 1,805m, Alternatives at USD 2,553m and assets under stake at USD 2,790m. The FY2025 10-K describes validator services to eleven blockchain networks and smart-contract deployments across more than 20. Named ETF partners include State Street Global Advisors, Invesco, DWS, CI Global Asset Management and Itaú; BlackRock selected Galaxy as an approved validator for its first rewards-generating crypto ETP in April 2026, and Morgan Stanley Investment Management for new Ethereum and Solana ETPs in August 2026.
highlights: AUM plus assets under stake fell from about USD 12bn (31 December 2025) to USD 7.1bn (30 June 2026)
Adjusted gross profit from this segment is small and stable: USD 21m, USD 18m and USD 17m in the three quarters to Q2 2026
Galaxy retains between 5% and 10% of the blockchain rewards earned on third-party assets bonded to its validator nodes
Alluvial Finance acquired 25 November 2025 for USD 7.1m cash, making Galaxy the development company for Liquid Collective
Initial USD 75m closing of a tokenized CLO in January 2026, which Galaxy calls the first of its kind
The fee split between Galaxy and its ETF issuer partners is **explicitly not disclosed**
productsAndServices.positioning: The one ranked comparison located is an editorial list, not an industry league table, and it places Galaxy fifth of five at USD 12bn behind BlackRock (USD 51.9bn in IBIT alone), Grayscale, Bitwise and Fidelity — and that figure is now stale by roughly 40%. The Invesco Galaxy Bitcoin ETF holds about USD 516-526m against IBIT's USD 51.9bn, about 1% of the leader. No genuine digital-asset AUM league table including Galaxy could be found.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Sub-advisory and partnership arrangements with established asset managers; direct fund management; validator services to custodians and institutions.
productsAndServices.roadmap: State Street Galaxy Onchain Liquidity Sweep Fund; a USD 125m onchain yield fund with SharpLink announced 7 August 2026; a multi-year BNY collaboration announced 4 August 2026 with Galaxy as design partner for staking on BNY's digital-asset custody platform.

productsAndServices.name: Treasury and Corporate
productsAndServices.description: The third reportable segment holds Galaxy's own digital assets, its venture and fund investments, and the legacy mining assets that were written down on the Helios conversion. It is where the losses sit: FY2025 segment net loss of USD 434.1m against Digital Assets' USD 193.9m profit. Net digital-asset and investment exposure was about USD 2.1bn at 30 September 2025 and USD 1,160m at Q2 2026. Largest disclosed investments at 31 December 2025 were bitcoin and ether spot ETFs (USD 535.8m), limited-partner interests in Galaxy-sponsored funds (USD 259.3m), Ripple Labs (USD 217.1m) and Forward Industries (USD 88.2m).
highlights: FY2025 impairment of digital assets: USD 753.7m, against USD 331.9m in FY2024
Mining equipment and related infrastructure impaired by USD 87.3m in FY2025 on the Helios conversion, plus USD 12.3m of disposals
Proprietary mining revenue fell 77% to USD 14.5m in FY2025 and ceased at the end of Q1 2025
Cash and stablecoins of USD 2,459m at Q2 2026 (USD 896m cash plus USD 1,563m stablecoins)
productsAndServices.positioning: This segment is what makes Galaxy's reported earnings swing with the crypto market irrespective of how the trading desk or the data centre performed, and it is the clearest reason a reader should not treat consolidated net income as a measure of either operating business.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Not disclosed as a growth business.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess that Galaxy is a financial institution that owns a data centre, not a data-centre company with a trading desk, and that the mismatch with its `developer` classification is real rather than cosmetic. Basis: the SEC classifies the registrant under SIC 6211, Security Brokers, Dealers and Flotation Companies. FY2025 revenue of USD 60,406.7m is recognised gross on a principal basis with USD 60,175.8m of offsetting transaction expense — the company's own 10-K warns that this 'overshadow[s] other parts of the business'. Its disclosed concentrations are trading-platform and lending-counterparty concentrations, not tenant concentrations. Its regulated subsidiaries are three broker-dealers, an investment adviser, a swap dealer and money-services businesses. The data-centre segment produced USD 20m of adjusted gross profit in Q2 2026 against USD 49m from Global Markets.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess that the three power numbers published for Helios are routinely conflated in outside reporting and that only one of them is contracted. Basis: 1.63 GW is ERCOT-approved, LLIS-complete and utility-contracted; **800 MW gross / 526 MW of critical IT load is leased to CoreWeave**; and 133 MW of critical IT was delivered at 30 June 2026. The FY2025 10-K states plainly that 'the remaining 830 MW of approved power capacity remains available to be contracted'. The gross-to-critical-IT ratio on this campus is about 1.52:1, so a headline of '800 MW' overstates sellable IT load by roughly half.

3. **(High confidence)** We assess that Galaxy publishes no all-phase base-term contract value, and that the absence is what makes cross-company lease comparisons in this cohort unsound. Basis: the only aggregates Galaxy publishes across all three phases are **average annual** figures — 'over USD 1bn' from August 2025, raised to 'USD 1.2bn+' in the Q2 2026 release. Base-term totals exist only per phase: about USD 4.5bn of total lease payments for Phase I and USD 10.4bn of minimum contracted lease payments for Phase II, with no Phase III equivalent published. The audited ASC 842 figure is different again at USD 4,747.8m of total future minimum lease income at 30 June 2026. Peers publish 15-year base-term aggregates (Hut 8 USD 26.6bn, Applied Digital about USD 36bn); Galaxy publishes an annual rate. The two are not the same measure and cannot be ranked against each other.

4. **(High confidence)** We assess that the lessor accounting is the single most consequential technical fact about this business and that it is new. Basis: the Q2 2026 10-Q added an accounting policy that did not exist in the FY2025 10-K, classifying the CoreWeave arrangements as **operating leases under ASC 842**, with lease income recognised straight-line and consideration allocated between lease and non-lease components. The consequences are visible: the campus stays in Property and equipment (USD 2,218.2m at 30 June 2026) rather than becoming a lease receivable; there is no day-one gain; and a USD 150.0m prepayment received in FY2025 was **still sitting in deferred revenue at 30 June 2026**, unrecognised, even though rent had commenced. A sales-type classification would have produced a materially different earnings profile from identical cash flows.

5. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that Galaxy's cost of data-centre capital is materially higher than its peers' and that single-tenant credit is the reason. Basis: the Phase II notes priced at **9.875%** in July 2026. In the same market Cipher issued Amazon-guaranteed paper at 6.125% in February 2026 and Google-backstopped paper at 7.125% in November 2025, and Hut 8's River Bend bond priced at 6.192% with BBB- ratings. Galaxy's tenant is CoreWeave, unrated and levered, and no credit enhancement behind the lease is disclosed. The 10-K's own risk factor concedes the dependence on 'a single customer' whose contract expires in 2040 and which 'may terminate its agreement with us in certain circumstances, including if we fail to achieve certain milestones'.

6. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the asset-management franchise is contracting rather than growing, and that outside rankings of it are stale. Basis: combined assets under management and assets under stake fell from about USD 12bn at 31 December 2025 to **USD 7.1bn at 30 June 2026**, a fall of roughly 40% in six months. The most-cited external ranking places Galaxy fifth of five US crypto asset managers at the USD 12bn figure, which is now wrong. The Invesco Galaxy Bitcoin ETF holds about USD 516-526m against BlackRock's IBIT at about USD 51.9bn. No genuine industry league table of digital-asset managers that includes Galaxy could be located.

7. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that key-person exposure here is legal as much as operational, and that the company says so itself. Basis: the 10-K names Michael Novogratz in its key-person risk factor and adds a second, unusual one — that 'our Founder has been a vocal and visible proponent of digital assets, in some cases attracting controversy' and that this makes material regulatory scrutiny foreseeable 'irrespective of whether we have engaged in any unlawful conduct'. The New York Attorney General's LUNA case turned on his personal promotion of the token, and he is a named individual defendant in the Ontario class action certified on 27 August 2026. He held about 49.25% of total voting power at 2 April 2026 and his board seat derives from a nomination agreement with an entity he controls.

8. **(Low confidence)** We assess that the market has not settled on how to value the company and that the disagreement is about which business it is. Basis: Citizens split its target roughly USD 25 a share for Digital Assets against more than USD 35 for Data Centers — i.e. the data centre is worth more than the original firm — while Piper Sandler attributed about USD 28 of a USD 42 target to Helios and simultaneously valued the whole on about 15 times 2027 estimated adjusted gross profit, a financials methodology. Maxim's thesis rests on the digital-asset business instead. Zacks classifies it under Financial - Miscellaneous Services and downgraded it to Strong Sell in July 2026 while Morgan Stanley raised its target to USD 48 in September 2026. Sixteen analysts average about USD 40 with a range of USD 25 to USD 57.

**Collection gap:** Galaxy publishes no Phase III base-term dollar figure, no Phase III capex, and no yield on cost other than Phase II's 13.7%. The ETF fee split with issuer partners is explicitly not disclosed. AUM is not broken out below the ETFs / Alternatives / assets-under-stake split. The company publishes no photographs of any executive or director. investor.galaxy.com and SEDAR+ were both unreachable during this research, so anything Galaxy has filed only in Canada — including the original 28 March 2025 Phase I lease announcement, which is absent from the company's own newsroom archive — is outside this dossier. Finally, the FY2025 10-K's account of the Ontario class action is superseded: it describes the matter as uncertified with a hearing scheduled for June 2026, and certification was granted on 27 August 2026.

relationships.scale: 800 MW gross / 526 MW critical IT across three phases; >USD 1.2bn anticipated average annual revenue
relationships.via: Helios data-centre campus, Dickens County, Texas
relationships.note: The sole tenant of the entire contracted capacity at Helios, across three 15-year leases.
relationships.context:
CoreWeave leases all 800 MW of gross power and 526 MW of critical IT load currently contracted at Helios, in three phases on identical terms: 15-year base leases with two five-year extension options, a 3.0-5.0% CPI-linked escalator and a near-triple-net structure. Phase I (133 MW critical IT) was fully delivered by 30 June 2026 and is expected to run at about USD 80m of quarterly leasing revenue from Q3 2026; Phase II (260 MW, lease dated 8 August 2025) delivers from Q2 2027; Phase III (133 MW, lease entered January 2026) in 2028.

The exposure is total and Galaxy discloses it as such: 'We expect that our AI/HPC data center business will initially be highly dependent on a single customer, CoreWeave, and may continue to derive a significant portion of the revenue of our Data Centers operating business segment from such single customer for the foreseeable future.' The initial contract expires in 2040, and the tenant may terminate in defined circumstances including a failure to hit construction milestones.

No credit enhancement behind the tenant is disclosed — no parent guarantee, no third-party backstop. That is the material difference from Cipher (Amazon.com, Inc. guaranty) and Hut 8 (a Google backstop at River Bend), and it is visible in the pricing: Galaxy's Phase II notes carry a 9.875% coupon against Cipher's 6.125% on Amazon paper.

relationships.scale: service agreement for the incremental 830 MW; campus total 1.63 GW approved
relationships.note: Utility counterparty for Helios's incremental approved capacity, alongside Wind Energy Transmission Texas as transmission interconnection provider.
relationships.context:
Galaxy executed a service agreement with AEP Texas Inc. for the additional 830 MW approved by ERCOT on 15 January 2026, which doubled total approved capacity at Helios to over 1.6 GW. Wind Energy Transmission Texas, LLC is the transmission interconnection provider and facilitated the large-load interconnection studies — a steady-state study and a stability study. Galaxy funds and owns its own private substation and connects front-of-the-meter to the ERCOT grid.

The relationship now runs through a regulatory bottleneck: Galaxy's Q2 2026 10-Q discloses that the Texas Governor's August 2026 directive requires the PUCT and ERCOT to complete a verification and audit of every data centre in the interconnection process before any project moves forward, and that this 'may impact the power approval timelines for certain of our data center sites'.

relationships.note: General contractor on Helios Phase II, mobilised on site since April 2026.
relationships.context: HITT Contracting is the general contractor for Helios Phase II — the 400 MW gross / 260 MW critical IT project financed by the USD 3.507bn senior secured notes — and has been mobilised on site since April 2026, with earthwork complete and structural foundations under way as of the Q2 2026 report. Data-hall deliveries are expected to commence in Q2 2027. HITT's own dossier makes no claim about Galaxy, so this edge is recorded from Galaxy's side only.

relationships.note: Both let large Texas campuses to single tenants; the counterparty credit is opposite.
relationships.context:
Cipher Digital and Galaxy compete for ERCOT interconnection capacity and for the same tenant demand, and both campuses began as bitcoin mining sites. The credit structures are opposites: roughly two-thirds of Cipher's contracted revenue carries an Amazon.com, Inc. guarantee, while 100% of Galaxy's contracted capacity sits with unrated CoreWeave and carries no disclosed enhancement. The bond market prices the difference at 375 basis points — Cipher's Black Pearl notes at 6.125% against Galaxy's Helios Phase II notes at 9.875%.

The deeper difference is that Cipher is a pure landlord in run-off from mining, while Galaxy is a securities firm for which the campus is one segment of three.

relationships.note: Peer Texas landlord; Hut 8's Beacon Point campus base-term value is the single figure most often mistaken for a three-company total.
relationships.context:
Hut 8 and Galaxy both operate large single-tenant Texas campuses financed with ring-fenced project debt. Hut 8 publishes a company-wide base-term contract value of USD 26.6bn across 949 MW of contracted critical IT, and a Beacon Point campus figure of USD 19.6bn; Galaxy publishes no comparable base-term aggregate at all, only an average annual figure of more than USD 1.2bn. The two cannot be ranked against each other without restating one of them.

On counterparty credit Hut 8 markets investment-grade tenants and holds a Google backstop at River Bend; Galaxy discloses neither for CoreWeave.

relationships.note: Peer converted-miner landlord, with a 20-year lease term against Galaxy's 15.
relationships.context: TeraWulf leases to Fluidstack with Google backstops and, separately, holds an Anthropic lease at Hawesville, Kentucky reported at about USD 19bn over a **20-year** initial term. That term difference alone makes a headline-value comparison with Galaxy's 15-year leases misleading, which is the general problem with ranking this cohort by contract value.

relationships.note: The other large landlord whose contracted capacity depends on CoreWeave.
relationships.context: Core Scientific and Galaxy share the same principal tenant. Core Scientific's CoreWeave contract runs about USD 10.2bn over twelve years alongside an AMD arrangement above USD 14bn, giving it a second anchor Galaxy does not have. For the ecosystem the more important point is the shared exposure: a CoreWeave credit event would reach Core Scientific, Applied Digital and Galaxy at once.

relationships.note: Peer landlord, also anchored on CoreWeave, publishing a base-term aggregate where Galaxy publishes an annual rate.
relationships.context: Applied Digital reports about USD 36bn of total contracted long-term lease value across roughly 1.4 GW of critical IT on a 15-year base-term basis, with about USD 86bn quoted including renewals. Galaxy's comparable disclosure does not exist: it publishes per-phase base-term figures and an all-phase average annual figure, so the two companies' headline numbers measure different things.

relationships.note: The vertically integrated comparator — IREN operates compute rather than leasing space.
relationships.context: IREN runs GPU clusters as a cloud business alongside its landlord role, anchored on Microsoft. The Futurum Group's contracted-revenue-per-megawatt measure — the one cross-operator ranking located for this cohort — puts IREN highest at about USD 40m per MW and Galaxy second at about USD 29m per MW, ahead of CoreWeave itself at about USD 28m. That measure is relayed second-hand and its term basis is not held constant across the companies compared.

relationships.note: Private energy-first developer competing for the same Texas power positions.
relationships.context: Crusoe builds and operates AI campuses on an energy-first thesis and discloses roughly 4.9 GW contracted across a much larger pipeline, but publishes no contract values. It competes with Galaxy for ERCOT capacity and for neocloud tenants without being comparable on any published financial measure.

relationships.note: Neocloud peer of Galaxy's tenant rather than of Galaxy itself — included because the tenant layer is where the credit risk sits.
relationships.context: Nebius is one of the neoclouds competing with CoreWeave for the AI compute demand that ultimately pays Galaxy's rent. Galaxy has no relationship with Nebius; the edge records that Galaxy's single-tenant exposure is exposure to competition at a layer it does not control. Galaxy's own July 2026 investor presentation characterises CoreWeave's position using CoreWeave's public filings — a USD 99.4bn contracted revenue backlog at Q1 2026 and an NVIDIA equity stake of about 11.5% — which is the company underwriting its tenant's competitive position in public.

relationships.note: Named together in the Texas Governor's data-centre standards release of 13 August 2026.
relationships.context:
Galaxy and Compass Datacenters were named together, with Montera Infrastructure, in the Texas Governor's release announcing commitments to comply with his data-centre standards. The release identifies Galaxy only by that single word; the identification as Galaxy Digital Inc. rests on Texas construction records naming Galaxy Helios II LLC of 300 Vesey Street, New York as owner of the Helios 2 and Helios 3 projects in Dickens County, and on the absence of any other Texas data-centre developer of that name.

Both compete for ERCOT interconnection capacity and hyperscale demand, from opposite kinds of business: Compass is a sponsor-owned build-to-suit landlord, Galaxy a securities broker-dealer for which the campus is one segment of three.

policyExposure.regime: PUCT / ERCOT data-centre verification and audit (Abbott directive)
policyExposure.exposure: Galaxy's Q2 2026 10-Q states that 'in August 2026, the Governor of Texas directed the Public Utility Commission of Texas and ERCOT to conduct a comprehensive verification and audit of all data centers advancing through ERCOT's interconnection process, and PUCT and ERCOT must complete this audit before any data center project moves forward. This review may impact the power approval timelines for certain of our data center sites.' The exposure bears on the 830 MW of approved but unleased Helios capacity, on the Helios III and Helios IV load requests of 1 GW each, and on the Merlin, Caspian and Selene sites.
policyExposure.mitigation: Galaxy issued a public statement on 7 August 2026 supporting the directive and committing that 'during declared emergency conditions, Helios will respond as required by SB-6'. It was named in the Governor's 13 August 2026 release as committing to comply with the state's data-centre standards.

policyExposure.regime: Texas SB 6 large-load rules and the ERCOT 75 MW threshold
policyExposure.exposure: Helios operates entirely front-of-the-meter on the ERCOT grid through a Galaxy-owned private substation, with AEP Texas as the utility and Wind Energy Transmission Texas as the transmission interconnection provider. Galaxy's Q2 2026 release describes capacity in ERCOT's own terms — 'Batch Zero Base Load' (signed interconnection agreements plus posted financial security) and 'Batch Zero Studied Load'. The McGregor announcement references coordinating with the utility 'to support development above the 75 MW large load threshold in ERCOT'.
policyExposure.mitigation: Galaxy funds and owns its own electrical infrastructure rather than relying on utility capital, and has committed Helios to emergency-condition response under SB 6.

policyExposure.regime: Digital-asset securities and commodities regulation (SEC, CFTC)
policyExposure.exposure: Galaxy operates a Token Committee of senior executives that classifies digital assets as 'No Restrictions' (US-tradable) or 'Non-U.S.', requiring a third-party assessment of federal securities-law status and a New York state securities-law assessment before transacting; the approved token list was published as an appendix to its December 2025 prospectus. Galaxy Derivatives LLC is a registered swap dealer and the company states it 'experienced a significant increase in costs to appropriately comply with swap dealer requirements'. The 10-K concedes that 'legal and regulatory risk will be an inherent feature of our business model until greater legal and regulatory certainty becomes possible'.

Galaxy's FY2025 10-K describes the GENIUS Act, signed into law in July 2025, as establishing 'the first comprehensive regulatory scheme for payment stablecoins in the United States'. The Q2 2026 10-Q adds that implementing rules and supervisory expectations from the federal banking agencies are being applied, and pairs it with the EU Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation. The exposure is direct: Galaxy held USD 1,563m of stablecoins at 30 June 2026, more than its USD 896m of cash.

policyExposure.regime: NYDFS BitLicense and state money-transmission licensing
policyExposure.exposure: At the date of the FY2025 10-K, 'neither Galaxy nor any of its affiliates currently have a BitLicense'. On 18 May 2026 the New York State Department of Financial Services granted GalaxyOne Prime NY a BitLicense and a Money Transmission License. Galaxy now describes a footprint of more than 50 global licences across three continents, including an FCA-licensed UK entity, registration under the Bahamas DARE Act 2024, and an ADGM office opened in December 2025. California's Digital Financial Assets Law required licensing from 1 July 2026, and at the 10-K date Galaxy had not applied but expected to.
policyExposure.mitigation: Galaxy secured the NYDFS licences before launching GalaxyOne's New York offering and holds an active lending licence in California.

policyExposure.regime: Dual US and Canadian reporting obligations
policyExposure.exposure: Galaxy voluntarily delisted from the Toronto Stock Exchange on 19 March 2026 but remains a reporting issuer in Canada, supervised by the Canadian Securities Administrators including the Ontario Securities Commission and filing on SEDAR. The 10-K names the resulting dual compliance burden as a risk. The Ontario Superior Court of Justice is also the forum for the securities class action certified against the company on 27 August 2026.

policyExposure.regime: New York Attorney General settlement — compliance undertakings
policyExposure.exposure: Galaxy settled with the New York Attorney General on 27 March 2025 over its promotion and sale of LUNA, for USD 200m undiscounted payable across 2025 to 2028, neither admitting nor denying. Beyond the money the settlement imposed compliance enhancements covering the company's public statements about cryptocurrency and its own purchases and sales — an ongoing constraint on how a firm whose founder is its most visible marketing asset may speak. A legal provision of USD 151m remained on the balance sheet at 31 December 2025.

financials.commentary: Galaxy reports in USD, so the normalized-KPI overlay is 'as reported'. **The revenue line requires a warning before it can be used at all.** Galaxy trades digital assets as principal and therefore recognises the gross proceeds of every sale as revenue, with an almost exactly offsetting cost in Transaction expenses — FY2025 revenue of USD 60,406.7m against transaction expenses of USD 60,175.8m. The company's own 10-K states that 'the magnitude of changes in Revenue on the Company's statement of operations overshadow other parts of the business, but are predominantly offset by Transaction expenses in Net income'. The `kpi: revenue` overlay below is set because it is the company's reported total revenue for the whole company, which is what the field means; a consumer comparing it with an operating company's revenue is comparing turnover with rent and will be wrong by orders of magnitude. Galaxy's own preferred measures are adjusted gross profit and adjusted EBITDA, neither of which has a GAAP equivalent. A second caution: the reorganisation of 13 May 2025 was accounted for as a reverse recapitalisation with Galaxy Digital Holdings LP as accounting acquirer and predecessor, so comparative periods before that date are the partnership's. No US analyst consensus for FY2024 could be located — Galaxy was a Cayman-domiciled TSX issuer with no SEC domestic reporting until May 2025 — so no beat/miss verdict is offered for that year.

metrics.name: Share repurchases
metrics.actual: 2,966 thousand shares at an average of USD 20.50
metrics.result: The Q1 release states 3.2 million shares for USD 65m; the 10-Q's own table implies about USD 60.8m. Both are published and neither is reconciled.

periods.commentary: The first quarter with data-centre revenue, and the smallest loss in four quarters. Phase I's 133 MW was fully in service by quarter end. Note the scale: USD 18.9m of leasing revenue inside USD 8.56bn of reported revenue.

metrics.name: Revenues
metrics.result: An 18.12% miss on a gross principal-basis line — informative about trading volumes, not about the business's earning power.

metrics.name: Data center leasing revenue
metrics.result: The first lease revenue Galaxy has ever recognised. A further USD 5.816m of data centers operator revenue was exactly offset by USD 5.816m of operator cost.

metrics.name: Diluted and adjusted EPS
metrics.result: A 75% beat on the Zacks consensus. A separate tracker reported the same quarter against a USD (0.46) estimate for an 80.5% beat — the panels disagree.

metrics.name: Adjusted gross profit / adjusted EBITDA
metrics.actual: USD 43m adjusted gross profit; USD (77)m adjusted EBITDA

metrics.name: Segment adjusted gross profit
metrics.actual: Global Markets USD 49m; Data Centers USD 20m; Asset Management and Infrastructure Solutions USD 17m
metrics.result: Data Centers is now the second-largest contributor, in its first quarter of operation.

metrics.name: Total assets
metrics.actual: USD 10,843.981m; total equity USD 2,720.108m; stockholders' equity USD 1,823.366m
metrics.result: Property and equipment net USD 2,218.204m; construction commitments outstanding USD 1,489.2m.

metrics.name: Notes payable
metrics.actual: USD 3,415.757m at 30 June 2026, excluding the USD 3,507m Helios Phase II notes issued on 28 July 2026
metrics.result: Comprising USD 445m of 2026 exchangeables, USD 1,268.257m due 2028 (the Helios I term loan), USD 402.5m of 2029 exchangeables and USD 1,300m of 2031 exchangeables.

metrics.name: Assets under management plus assets under stake
metrics.actual: USD 7.1bn — ETFs USD 1,805m, Alternatives USD 2,553m, assets under stake USD 2,790m
metrics.result: Down from about USD 12bn at 31 December 2025. Galaxy's own website reported USD 8bn of assets on platform and USD 4.4bn of AUM for the same date — the two disclosures do not agree.

metrics.name: Trading counterparties and loan book
metrics.result: Digital-asset loans receivable net of USD 786.680m against collateral payable of USD 983.122m.

metrics.name: Cash and stablecoins
metrics.actual: USD 2,459m — USD 896m of cash and USD 1,563m of stablecoins
metrics.result: More stablecoins than cash, which is itself a statement about the balance sheet.
